title: Geometric two-isomorphisms preserve the ordinary scalar balanced pairing
statement:
Let $C,D$ be sites small in the universe of module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I,J:\operatorname{Sh}(C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(D)$ be inverse-image functors of geometric morphisms, that is finite-limit-preserving left adjoints [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and fix a natural isomorphism $\theta:I\xrightarrow{\sim}J$. Let $a:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of discrete commutative rings, with constant ring sheaves $R_C,R_D$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $I_R,J_R$ be the module lifts obtained by applying $I,J$ to addition and scalar multiplication and identifying the inverse images of $R_C$ with $R_D$ by their canonical constant-section identifications. Then $\theta$ induces $R_D$-linear natural isomorphisms $\theta^R:I_R\xrightarrow{\sim}J_R$. Under the canonical constant-ring identifications its components on $A_C,B_C$ are identities and commute with $a$.

Write $E_C=B_C\otimes_{A_C}-$ and $E_D=B_D\otimes_{A_D}-$ for sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $e_I:I_BE_C\xrightarrow{\sim}E_DI_A$ and $e_J:J_BE_C\xrightarrow{\sim}E_DJ_A$ be the canonical scalar/pullback isomorphisms normalized by scalar insertion and the generalized pure-tensor formula [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison, lem-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison-construction]. For every $A_C$-module sheaf $N$, one has
$$e_{J,N}\circ\theta^B_{E_CN}=E_D(\theta^A_N)\circ e_{I,N}.$$
For the universal balanced pairing $q:B_C\times N\to B_C\otimes_{A_C}N$, the underlying equality before passage to its tensor quotient is
$$\theta_{B_C\otimes_{A_C}N}\circ I(q)=J(q)\circ(\theta_{B_C}\times\theta_N).$$
The induced map of the scalar-extended modules is $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes\theta_N(m)$ on generalized pure tensors, with their balancing relations. These assertions hold for the module sheafifications, not merely on global constant sections [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $I$ and $J$ are specified composites of geometric inverse images, the same equation holds with $e_I,e_J$ expanded as their iterated normalized scalar/pullback maps under the canonical ordinary module composition identifications. It also holds termwise and naturally for cochain complexes and chain maps [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules].

source.place: Tag 03EL, label lemma-tensor-product-pullback, proof: naturality of the balanced pairing. The compatibility with a specified geometric 2-isomorphism and its expanded composite presentations is the agent-formulated extraction of old proof steps 1–2.

proof.text: Write $1_C,1_D$ for the terminal sheaves. Since $I$ and $J$ preserve finite limits, $I1_C$ and $J1_C$ are terminal and $\theta_{1_C}$ is their unique comparison. For any sheaves $X,Y$, naturality at the two projections says that, under the canonical product comparisons, both projections of $\theta_{X\times Y}$ equal those of $\theta_X\times\theta_Y$. The product universal property gives $\theta_{X\times Y}=\theta_X\times\theta_Y$. This also applies to products with the coefficient sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, balanced-pairing argument; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, universal characterization

proof.text: The set constant sheaf of a set R is the coproduct of R copies of the constant singleton sheaf: construct the scalar-labelled cofan in Type and apply the constant-sheaf functor. The constantCommuteCompose isomorphism identifies its inclusions with scalarSection for the underlying constant commutative ring sheaf. Each path inverse preserves this coproduct, by induction using its steps’ adjunctions and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. The constant singleton is terminal, and the comparison on it is unique. Induct the scalar-section normalization of each step along a path. Naturality of theta on every inclusion and the colimit universal property then give both coefficient identities. Naturality of constantCommuteCompose in a gives scalarSection(r) followed by a equal to scalarSection(a(r)); applying the same colimit uniqueness proves compatibility of every path coefficient comparison with a. These are equalities of sheaves, not a test on global sections.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi; coproduct uniqueness and naturality

proof.text: Use the algebraic module lifts stored in each Step, as defined by [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Induction along each Path transports their generalized addition, scalar-action and zero graph equations to the iterated underlying comparisons. Applying these equations to the universal operand products gives the binary-operation comparison equations. Naturality of theta on these operation maps and on both projections, together with the coefficient identities of step 2, makes the conjugated underlying module map additive and linear. Package it as a module map. These module maps are natural by faithfulness of the underlying functor, and are isomorphisms because that functor reflects isomorphisms. This constructs the required thetaA and thetaB with the stipulated underlying equations.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi, module operations; naturality at the operations

proof.text: Put $T=E_CN$ and let $q:B_C\times N\to T$ be the actual sheaf tensor pairing. Naturality at this sheaf map gives $\theta_T I(q)=J(q)\theta_{B_C\times N}$. By step 1 this is precisely $\theta_T I(q)=J(q)(\theta_{B_C}\times\theta_N)$, the requested equation before tensor quotient. The operation equations of step 3 imply that the pairing $(b,m)\mapsto b\otimes\theta^A_N(m)$ is additive in both entries and balanced: $a(r)b\otimes\theta^A_N(m)=b\otimes r\theta^A_N(m)=b\otimes\theta^A_N(rm)$. The scalar-extension functor on this map is therefore $E_D(\theta^A_N)$, by the pure-tensor characterization of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus].

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, balanced-pairing argument; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, universal characterization

proof.text: The generalized pure-tensor normalization is part of each supplied Step. First establish its iterated form by the induction of step 7. Applying that form to the actual sheaf scalar pairing gives the entire pairing comparison equation, using the product comparison and the two underlying identifications. Conjugate the two sides of the desired square by eI inverse. After precomposition with the target scalar pairing, step 4, coefficient rigidity, and the two module-isomorphism underlying equations identify the sides. Cancel the product and underlying isomorphisms. The module sheafification adjunction and sectionwise extension-of-scalars hom_ext show that linear maps agreeing on this pairing are equal. Cancel eI inverse to obtain the desired square. Only the supplied normalized comparisons are used; no comparison is selected using an existence theorem.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, balanced-pairing argument; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, universal characterization

proof.text: The pure-tensor argument takes place in sheaves. Indeed the tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor presheaf. On a test object, the balanced formula in step 4 defines a linear map on that sectionwise tensor and commutes with restrictions. The factorization and uniqueness in [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extend it uniquely to the sheafified tensor. Thus equality on these pairings proves equality of sheaf maps even when a tensor section is not globally a pure tensor. In the coordinates of $e_I,e_J$, the induced map is exactly $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes\theta_N(m)$.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, balanced-pairing argument; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, universal characterization

proof.text: Prove the generalized normalization for a Path by induction. For the empty path it is the given formula itself, since all comparisons are identities. For cons s p, first apply s.normalized to get the intermediate pairing formula on s.inverse(Z); then apply the induction hypothesis to that whole sheaf and its three resulting maps. Naturality of p.rightUnderlying inverse at s.comparison moves the intermediate comparison through p.inverse. The resulting expression is exactly Path.comparison with its displayed associators. This proves the square for the actual expanded comparisons, without replacing the supplied paths or maps.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, balanced-pairing argument; Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product, universal characterization

proof.text: Induction along paths also transports the generalized zero graph equations of the algebraic lifts. Naturality of their underlying comparisons then shows the left and right module path functors preserve zero morphisms. Scalar extension preserves zero morphisms because tensorAdjunction makes it a left adjoint. Thus both functors in the complex clause admit the required PreservesZeroMorphisms instances. Naturality of the square is equality of the corresponding natural transformations, by evaluation at each module. Apply NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex to that equality for ComplexShape.up Z to get the stated termwise and chain-map-natural equation, with no boundedness hypothesis.
